correctness.rationale: Since the zero set V0 is not dominating, some positive vertex x has no zero neighbor. When V0 is nonempty, the universal center cannot play x, so x lies in a blade B_i, forcing center positive and all r blade vertices positive. Weight ≥r+1, and r+1 fails Italian domination on every all-zero other blade (they see center label1 only). A matching construction with center2 and B_i labels1 gives weight r+2. If optimum weight r+2 had center1, at most one further positive unit outside the forced blade is available; m≥3 guarantees at least one totally zero other blade, whose zero vertices have total neighbor weight1, contradiction. Thus center2 and exactly one full blade1 are forced, giving m distinct functions for every r≥1. Independently enumerated all 3^(1+mr) labels for (3,1),(3,2),(3,3),(4,1),(4,2),(5,1), reproducing minima r+2 and multiplicity m; finite checks only corroborate arbitrary m,r proof.
